title: Not a great app
body:
A self-care app should help you recover after a rough day—not make you feel guilty for having one. Losing a streak or seeing your pet react to missed check-ins can turn “support” into another obligation. 

I used to really love Finch, but lately it no longer feels like a “feel-good” app to me. I don’t believe people should face consequences or lose progress simply because life gets busy and they miss a day. A self-care app should offer encouragement and understanding—not leave someone feeling guilty or punished for needing a break.

title: Potential… but occasional annoyance
body:
Lots of great things about this app. However I’m having a couple of issues that are pushing me closer and closer to deleting my account. The first is that the app is constantly resetting my daily log in streak, despite the fact that I go on everyday… I can’t figure out if it’s a time zone thing wherever their office is, or if the app is just glitching. Normally I wouldn’t care except it’s now affecting if I get the micro pets from the events or not, because it’s saying I’m many days behind, when I know I open the app every day. Super weird. 

The second thing is the shop item rotation. My experience is that I get the same rotation of 4 collections over and over again, while the plus items are quite varied. I don’t know why I’m being shown dinosaur wallpaper and vegetable wallpaper every day for the 6th month in a row when there are SO many other wallpaper options. Same happens with every other item. Looking online it appears I’m not the only person feeling disenchanted by the game because of this. 

It’s a good game, but currently the glitches and lack of variation in the shop are making me feel like I don’t need this app anymore.

title: Great app! Make it even more helpful
body: This app has been a wonderful tool for both me and my husband as we navigate complex mental health journeys. My one suggestion would be to add the ability to set up two sets of goals: a good day and a complete non-functional day. My husband has set many goals that he enjoys achieving when he’s doing well, but on days when he’s not coping, Finch seems too overwhelming and he doesn’t open it. While it’s possible to snooze goals, going through the list one by one when you’re in that state is a lot of hard effort and decision-making. It would be great to be able to set up your essential list of ten goals for off days and then just toggle one switch to get that version.  I think it would help make these crashes shorter if you could celebrate with Finch that you ate something,  drank water and took your medication, and then go back to your full list of goals when you felt better.

title: Great… up until the events
body: Love this app a lot don’t get me wrong, and it was great for the first few weeks, but then the events started. Limited edition pets, only come once, if you don’t meet the goalposts sorry you’re not getting it! For people who struggle with motivation or just forget to open the app the motive becomes to lie when you can’t do anything instead of taking a rest day. One lie snowballs into it becoming far too easy to click ‘completed’ when you didn’t. The scaling difficulty is alright in theory, but you should be able to set the pace yourself (i.e. select how many days before they level up) because for some it takes a bit more to adjust. Also, making additional goals completed a bit more rewarding would be nice, right now it removes about 10 minutes off an (at minimum) 6 hour quest per goal. Love this game, would recommend it, but if you’re someone who loses motivation easy it eventually becomes ‘must get the pets even if I didn’t complete my goals’. Would love if the timed events were just slightly rarer locations after the event ends so you can still get all the pets but it rewards you for doing it now. Anyways, great game but gonna have to leave it at 3 stars for how it lost its effectiveness.

title: Good at some things, ok at others...cons outweigh pros
body:
Let's start with the bad. My bird (birb is too cringe for me) hates nearly EVERYTHING. I wouldn't care if it was even 50/50, but 90% of the things my bird encounters he either dislikes or hates. He even doesn't like the discoveries that don't count (based on what he says)!

I think it goes against self-care and mental health wellness when your virtual pet is so incredibly negative, and you're eventually trying to choose an answer as if it's a puzzle instead of it just being natural.

The community also isn't great, especially if you have negative feedback (although in-app you can only send gifts and greetings/likes to each other).


In terms of ok, I'd say the app itself. There are clothing and feather colours for your bird, tasks to check, pets for your bird, furniture to use in your home and you can explore locations based on real life.

That all sounds fine on paper, but the clothing often looks strange considering the bird's shape, the home is a single angle that you can't do anything in (other than have your bird sit on the bed at night, and decorate in specific ways) and the pets are only there to follow your bird. The exploration is simply checking off tasks and waiting for the next discovery popup to unlock, and gaining some trivia from it when the bird isn't bashing things. Or during.


For the good...the game is cute overall, you can now (recently) get a subcription for a low price, I was given a lifetime subscription for free, it's easy to use, the UI is clean and easy to navigate (although why do I have to go into each category to sell items from there? why not just have a sell menu for everything on one page?) and the writing activities are a good introduction to journalling (despite no line breaks).

EDIT: The "lifetime" subscription expires in a year.

title: Such an amazing app.
body:
People will tell you that this app is bad, or annoying, or tacky, but it is seriously wonderful. It’s so inclusive (which I seriously appreciate so much.), it’s easy to use, it’s fun, and it keeps you wanting to do your next job. To simply put it, people who just click tasks when they don’t do them, don’t need the app and it’s not for them. But, if you struggle with doing things this might help you! But don’t just tap through everything, actually do the thing. It’s so rewarding, and it makes your birb so happy! 
This app has been a great way for me to socialize with people, and that’s something that can be hard at times, so is such a great way to get a conversation going. I have so many friends that use it! In fact I’m almost running out of room on my tree! It’s so wonderful, and I can’t wait to keep using it in the future. I’ve been using this app for a year and a half I think now? Two years? And every time I log in, it makes me so happy. 
Thank you finch team!

title: Worth the download
body:
I had a friend suggest this app to me a few years ago and I ignored them. 1 month ago I downloaded it. I am using the free version. 

I thought some of the self care suggestions to do daily were silly and a bit ‘too easy’ or not relevant to me so I added some of my own productivity tasks to them. I noticed just by sticking to doing a few home cleaning things a day like ending the day with wiping my counters that it was making a difference to my home being tidier and my brain feeling calmer. It was also wiring something in my brain to show me that it feels good to complete simple tasks. 

Then I started enjoying doing the self care stuff like the breathing exercises it suggests and filling out the reflection questions. 

I love that you get rainbow coins everyday for completing tasks, and for simply signing in. I love that you can purchase something from the shop everyday. Really helps for ppl that have a shopping addiction, as you get satisfaction for that, without actually spending money. 

Overall I think this app is wonderful! Thank you for not having annoying ads. I’m hopeful that you won’t ever have to introduce those. I don’t really want to pay for a monthly or yearly subscription but if there was ever an option to pay a one time fee and get some sort of lasting perk (maybe allow for more breathing exercises to be unlocked??) I would do that because I would love to support the app makers for such a wonderful app that has brought me joy and calm daily.

I do wish the app itself could handle having more friends. I’m on page two and I am already feeling a little glitchy on the friend page. My other friend has SO many friends that sometimes it takes a minute for the app to load to the next page or do anything. It’s not their phone as when they get out of Finch it’s fast and not glitchy. It’s the app that can’t handle the amount of friends they have. So it would be amazing if the developers to Finch could increase the capacity the app could handle for friends OR put a cap on the friend limit. Other than that, it’s a great app and I love it a lot!

title: I LOVE THIS APP SO MUCH!!!
body: THIS IS SUCH AN AMAZING APP! I love this app, I love that you can have it as a widget on your Home Screen and you have a daily streak which is something that really encourages me to use the app more. I also love that you can name your finch and choose its pronouns, but I also appreciate that the finches have their own personalities and their own personal preferences. I find it so fun to dress up the finches and that you can change their colours and their homes. The micro pets are so cute and I think that it’s so cool that there is a toggle on the micro pets profile so that you can prevent them from growing to an adult and so you can keep the pets as babies. There is also no ads which is amazing considering that it’s completely free to download and all of the in-app purchases are not thrown in your face, in like most free apps. It is so great that you can also have your friends on the app so you can send them “good vibes” it’s really nice that your finch can go to real world places and go on adventures and learn things about where they are visiting. Overall this app is so amazing and I would 100% recommend to anyone who asks about it. I got my friends into it and now they have longer streaks than me! Thank you so much to the creators of this app, you have really changed my life and my vein on the world; I find it so much easier to wake up in the morning and face whatever comes my way. THANK YOU!!

title: PLEASE DON'T WASTE YOUR TIME
body:
Don't waste hours nurturing and caring for a pet on an app that can just DELETE ALL OF YOUR DATA and not be able to retrieve it. 

I had been using Finch for almost a year under the Pro subscription. The app had helped me immensely with my mental health and organization around my home. 

Then one day when opening the app I get a message saying that my data has been corrupted. I contacted Finch's customer service and guess what their best offer was? Providing me with a coded list of all their inventory and saying that, if I start from scratch and create a new pet, they will give me 30 items back as long as I provide them with the correct item code. 

I must have had almost 300 items in my inventory, all my outfits had been carefully labelled and organized, as well as my house decorations. 

PLEASE don't waste your time on this app, I don't know what they are doing with their data centres but anyone can have their pet deleted at ANY TIME. 

And they will apologize and say there is nothing they can do. Thanks for making me waste countless hours of my life, Finch.

Like 1 and 3 minute breathing exercises instead of those and the 5 and 10 minute ones kind of thing. Certain things in the shop too. It has tests you can do to see if you have stress or depression, and exercises you can do to help deal with them as well as a hotline you can contact. Something i just discovered is the soundscapes, which you find in the activities section. It plays fully in the background with no ads, and theres lots of different kinds of sounds you can listen to, as well as how long you want to listen. You can also pause your progress in the app so you don’t have to feel guilty when you come back after not being able to do it for a while, and the conversations with the little birdie are adorable.

title: Great!!!
body:
This app is literally so amazing. 

I really love how there is LGBTQ clothing and all the clothes are so cute and silly. The only issue with the clothing is the dresses look sorta weird on my finch. I have to settle with skirts instead because the dresses look like jumpsuits.
You can also colour your finch if you didn’t like the colour you originally picked. I made my finch look like a silly penguin. 🐧 

Next is the actual finch. You can change its name and pronouns at anytime. It also has they/them pronouns available!! 

The actual features of the app are great. There are ‘goals’ that you have to complete throughout the day to get your lil finch going on an adventure. The adventures take about 6 hours, which is perfect if you go to school or work because once you come home, you can check up on your finch after those 6 hours and it will have a lil conversation with you! It will learn about the world and its likes and dislikes and it will earn some traits! 

There are also some ‘activities’ in the app like timers, soundscapes, and stuff like that. 
Also little writing segments so you can write about your day/week!

5/5 stars. No complaints.
-Elliott S 🐧

title: Why does this kid friendly app mention a sexual book?
body:
This game says it’s good for people 4 years or older, but today the daily adventure thingy was about the book fourth wing???!! 
 My bird said a quote from the book about dragons or something and then it said “ it’s from this book called fourth Wing, but I changed it, cheep! My other favourite quote from the book is, ‘Don’t borrow tomorrows trouble.” And the new discovery says “likes fourth wing”.  That seems innocent and a kid might think “oh this book is about dragons, I want to read it”
But if you do not know, fourth wing is a fantasy book with extremely explicit sexual scenes (that’s what it’s known for) it is not appropriate for children, so I don’t know why they would pick this book when so many kids play this game, and could ask their parent for this book, and if the parent hasn’t heard of it, then they could buy it not knowing the content and just assuming it’s a kid’s fantasy book. 
What are the intentions behind picking a sm*t book out of all the other books that they could have picked that are appropriate for all ages.  very disturbing. This game is extremely appealing to kids, My little cousin plays this.  this is not appropriate at all.

The key here is to build your pet, ie. you get rewarded with checking off your to-do list, so you can buy some furniture for ur pet. it’s like the life stimulation games you played when you were a kid(I played plenty and it’s so addictive). For people like me, engaging in a game experience is way more fun than just a plain, boring to-do list app! Finch truly stands out among all the work app. At the end of the day, what’s the point of living if we cannot have fun of it? Whoever developed this, thank you, thank you and thank you!

title: ME TIME
body: Finch is the app I open in the morning and throughout the day for some ME TIME! I love that it allows me to input my to-do list for the day, check in with my friends/accountability buddies and reflect on how I am feeling WHILE being able to visually see what habits aren’t sticking. I would agree that it’s not everyone’s cup of tea, but it has certainly helped me and a number of people I know. It’s a fun way to reward yourself for completing simple tasks. I do wish it would dig a little deeper sometimes… the reflection prompts are repetitive and there should really be an interactive component, a little like chat GPT, to really check-in. Overall, I am really happy with this app and pay for the full version as it works for me. Thanks developers!

body:

I also had the same 3 reminders the entire week and nothing else.. they were the following;

1- wake up
(Thanks for the reminder to wake up, glad I was able to keep being alive today)

2- brush my teeth

3- do something happy

title: Super helpful, and super cute!
body:
I find that finch has really helped me set good self-care goals, and has helped me improve self confidence and my emotional regulation. I enjoy writing reflections to ease my mind, or practice gratitude to try and shift to a more positive outlook.

I like that there are goals for everyone, no matter where you’re at, including things like “just make it through the day,” or “get out of bed,” for those who may be struggling with depression, but also goals in self kindness and relaxation to aid anxiety, and even more for productivity and movement, and etc. There’s something for everyone and their needs :) !

Also, as a bird lover, this game is adorable and I love my little finch. So cute! Being able to buy accessories and decorations for her is very motivating, haha.

Overall, love the app. Found out about it through friends and haven’t stopped since.

title: Best App EVER
body: I grew up playing games on first Gen iPod, others like PollyPocket.com, Sims, Nintendogs.. Finch brings me so much genuine joy that is so reminiscent of my childhood but also literally helping me build better habits. I love that you can add personal goals, I’ve told many people already that I don’t think I would’ve passed my board exams without adding “Study for 30 mins” & “Do Flash Cards 15 mins” per day. It’s helped me get super on top of my self care and self love habits.. more movement and flossing daily are my next to conquer … the breathing exercises are hard but incredible, as are the affirmations. author: Samitchman

title: The only app I can commit to using
body:
I have adhd and this app helps me commit to a daily routine better than anything I’ve tried in the past. It gamifies to-do lists but in a way that’s actually enjoyable, not cumbersome, and shame/guilt-free (the pet doesn’t shame you for missing milestones or neglecting yourself). It’s great that they do monthly events to keep it interesting, and its very kind of them to include enough in the free version that you don’t feel penalized for being poor. And the micro-pets are a great way to keep us motivated to stick to our goals every month, making it feel like “goals I want to achieve” instead of the usual: “goals I have to achieve or I’m a failure”.

I also love how finch works emotional well-being into the UI in a way that’s not so obvious to the user, making it natural for the end user to get emotional benefits from using the app without feeling infantilized or like the app is being condescending. I only missed my longest streak (199 days) because I got married and chose not to check in that weekend. My new streak is going strong and I look forward to beating my 199 day record! 🔥

P.S. for new users, I highly recommend finding a friend that could also benefit from an accountability buddy & recommending finch to them; I am much more successful returning daily when I have a friend who’s trying to do it too!

P.P.S. I also use this app as a way to connect with my young nephew who loves using the app each night and lives across the country. His mom and him use finch for his bedtime routine & it’s such a cute and passive way to connect long-distance with family! He loves when my bird comes to visit his birdhouse and when we go on walks together in the app ❤️

Thanks, Finch devs! You’ve made something really incredible and in such a humanitarian way! I hope you feel proud of what you’ve accomplished with this app. I recommend it to everyone I know lol

title: Broken for 2 years with no fix
body:
I was a big booster of this app in the early days and it helped me a lot in organizing my day. Then it glitched so the time in the app was off by an hour or two depending on the time changes, and I had set it up so the goals were organized by time. I have had back and forths with the support team every few months and they keep promising me they are looking into it and ask me to be patient. They asked me to send a file to them in January 2025 to debug, which I did, and follow up, and I was given the same troubleshooting instructions then just asked to be patient again.

The latest update has a different way to order goals in terms of times of day, except they are lumped in at the end under “anytime” now. So if I want to add a goal to go at the top, for the beginning of the day, I can’t. Any new goals are lumped in at “anytime” at the end. I emailed about this twice and was only given a generic explanation that it’s a new feature, no engagement with or problem solving around morning goals now being sorted past all the rest of the day’s goals. It was broken before, and is even more broken now. I can’t really use this app to organize my day — it’s a bird dressup game and maybe a checklist at best. And I am disappointed to have been led on in promising a solution to the timing issue for 2 years only to have it be made not better, but worse. 

The app was good when it worked, and support was helpful for small glitches, but it seems they’ve given up entirely on their promise to debug or follow up to make sure the app works for me again. They repeat in every email to be patient, but I never expected they’d take advantage of that patience for 2 years. It really spoils the positive feelings they are otherwise trying to cultivate here.

author: Maizly

title: Good idea, not executed well
body:
I love that this app made a fun self-care tool freely accessible to everyone. And I like that you can do it alongside friends as well. We need more things like this. However, there are some things about this app that are making me incredibly frustrated. For starters the my free trial stopped working after a few hours and I lost all the benefits that I should have been able to explore. Then when I tried to cancel the subscription something popped up and said something along the lines of “the request couldn’t be processed at this time”. It dod change after that to say the subscription is expiring soon so hopefully I won’t be charged anyway. 
The next thing is customizability of the bird. I often see a lot of cute things in the catalogue that you are just not able to get, and then I’m disappointed to see that all of the actual shop items that are in stock are things that I’m not interested in. And you only get six options like every 15 hours or something ridiculous like that. And you can use your stones to refresh your options, but every time you do it, it gets more and more expensive so then you end up spending your stones on refreshing options to hopefully find something that you want to customize your bird. 
I love my bird daughter Gilfie but it also takes way too long to age her. She’s going to be a baby for a full week? I want to be able to play with things and explore the app but there are options I can’t do because I am told she’s too young. 
The next thing is I sent my friend a micropet for signing up, but I don’t have one and can’t get one because nobody invited me. I want a cute little Griffin too. Or a hedgehog. I feel like I am being punished because I found the app on an instagram ad instead of having a friend invite me. I’ve been playing the game for three days and have completed pretty much all my tasks and only just found an egg yesterday that still has not hatched. I only managed to have one friend join out of the 7 invites I sent otherwise I could have a cow micropet, but I don’t really like that I don’t also have the same pet options for signing up that she got for being invited.

title: Gamify self care
body:
For kids AND old people lol
Love it
Give it a chance. It works. Evidenced based, CBT type gamified self care app. My therapist uses it now too and suggests it to their clients. ❤️‍🩹🫂

I am not the type to like these types of apps usually, but I have stuck to this for a year. I check in with it every day, reflect, set goals, do breathing exercises check off reminders and todos, and repeat affirmations. 
Then, most importantly , I send my little pal on trips around the world, buy outfits or items for my character, and raise micro pets 🤣

My son and my friend use it too, and like in Duo Lingo, you can encourage each other and send gifts. 

Some days my goals are as simple as “step outside my home”, on better days I tackle my todo list.  
The free acct is wonderful if you can’t afford the premium. 

I know it sounds daft but it does work.

title: ADHD and anxiety help

I have pretty bad adhd that gives me task paralysis so when I need to get stuff done it’s really hard too, but this app has helped me soo much because I want to see the bird grow and in order to do that I have to do my tasks. I also have pretty bad anxiety so there’s a lot of calming breathing and stuff to guide you through a panic attack, there also stuff for depression to make sure you stay safe and I really appreciate that. It’s also got a great community, like if you don’t have the money for the premium then you can see if you can get sponsored by someone who can then you get the premium for free, and that has really helped me out because there is some stuff in the reflections and breathing that you have to have premium to do that I wanted to do but couldn’t untill I got sponsored. So thank you to the person who sponsored me and thank you to this app for being the back bone of my life❤️❤️

title: Demande de version française de l’application /
body:
Hello,

First of all, I would like to thank you for the Finch app, which is a valuable tool and truly meets real needs in terms of mental and emotional well-being. However, I would like to bring your attention to an important point: the absence of a French version.

Given the large number of French-speaking users, particularly in Canada where French is an official language, it is unfortunate that the app does not currently offer this option. An application focused on mental health should be inclusive and accessible, especially when it asks personal questions related to stress, anxiety, or motivation.

I strongly believe that adding French (and ideally the three most widely used languages: English, French, and Spanish) would allow your app to reach a much broader audience and better reflect the cultural diversity of your users.

As it stands, someone who does not master English simply cannot benefit from Finch, which greatly limits its accessibility.

I sincerely encourage you to consider this update. I remain convinced that an app of Finch’s quality deserves to be accessible to as many people as possible.

Thank you for your attention.


With the number of users you have, it is quite unreasonable that no multilingual version is offered, at least in English, French, and Spanish.

title: Excellent and incredibly useful life app
body: I saw this app advertised and thought I’d check it out. I liked the concept of a kind of tamagotchi but animated, that grows and learns with you. Not only is it fun but it’s really great for mental health! I have ADHD and Bipolar which is a great double whammy! But the app helps with great sounds when you accomplish tasks which is great for a dopamine hit!  You can purchase items for your home, clothes for your birb. It’s a blast!  Also it can help you through the really difficult times with calming activities, reflections, quizzes, and even soundscapes for sleep! I use this every night. My partner and I both use the app and I enjoy when she’s in my “house”. You can even take your character on trips to different places. It’s a hoot! You can do so much with the app, it’s really fun. Is there a cost? Yes, however, it is free with the help of guardians. Guardians pay extra with the app to help people who may not be able to afford it. I’m a guardian and I’m glad I could do my part. What a novel concept! I really do love this app!!

title: Cute AND Fun-ctional!
body:
Some days we have all the energy in the world and can do all the things. 

 Some days we have no energy at all. And some days, we have even less energy than that.

 I’ve been using this app for a week now, and not only has it allowed me to chart my moods and emotions about them, mark and complete goals (and make it a cute tamagotchi-like game!) but overall, the *community* is just a beautiful place. The space the team has made for everyone is remarkable and such a wonderful sight to see, when days blur that line of “what is empathy and compassion?”, and humans just can’t seem to understand each other. Finch Team, thank you for all that you do, and I can’t wait to keep using this app and continuing to work on my self, my goals, and improving myself ❤️‍🩹♥️🧡 

When I can afford it, not only would I like to buy myself a subscription but I would like to gift some too 🥰💖

title: Pleasant surprise
body:
I was not expecting this app to do much for me but I am pleasantly surprised. I have adhd ofc, and this has been a great way for me to organize my week and stay consistent.

I love the fact that I can program certain chores for certain days, and I don’t have to remember them as I just set a reminder for it. It’s really convenient not having to type in all the plans for the day, every single day which makes it less overwhelming. You can set up self care/gratitude to complete as well and that’s exactly what I need rn. 

It’s encouraging to have these positive reminders on my phone, but it’s also really reaffirming to take breaks to stretch, affirm myself, say something I like about myself and something I did well. It’s overall helping to boost my self trust.

author: khb d

title: An Honest Review
body:
It’s cute. You take care of your little finch, you do your tasks and watch them grow. You can buy them furniture and clothes with the stones you save from completing tasks. You want to unlock more times? Buy the subscription. I don’t think it’s a money grab because they let you have access to the necessities, and is completely functional without the subscription. 
Why rate 2 stars? 
Because I was about a year into this app, and it was a good app. But somewhere along the line it kept corrupting my data. No issue, I got a back up. Right? Eventually my back up got corrupted too, leaving me with an empty shell of what once brought me joy. It’s like watching your house burn down, realizing that yes, you can start new, but it will never be the same. And I’m not willing to put in all the work I once did to watch it burn down again.
What this app brought was nice. It kept me in line of the things that needed to be done. But not having a proper way to save/access and having the app constantly crash is extremely frustrating and unreliable. 
In theory this game/self care app is nice, but there’s a lot more work that needs to be done. 
I’m personally very disappointed and will not be returning.

title: Not upfront about subscription plans.
body:
I like the app and even shared it with multiple people and my daughter. I think it can help greatly for people struggling to manage stress, anxiety & self care. I really wanted to use plus but in looking at subscriptions there are MANY costs for a 1 year subscription. When I contacted support they could not explain the cost differences. They range between $19.99 & $99.99 and include every price point in between. 
They just told me that $59.99 was the standard package. The other price points are subject to promotional availability or limited access. But it doesn’t state what’s included with each price option and customer support couldn’t tell me either. Those are the price options when I go to select a plan but I want to know what’s different between free, $19.99, $59.99, $99.99 and really every plan  in between.

title: A great tool for building habits—just wish the rewards stayed rewarding
body:
I’ve been using Finch daily for the past 26 days, and it’s genuinely helped me stay on track with my goals. As someone with ADHD, I tend to procrastinate or avoid tasks that don’t bring immediate satisfaction, and Finch gave me that little hit of motivation I needed—at least at first.

The daily check-ins, small quests, and virtual pet rewards worked really well in the beginning. I even tried the Plus version (which I don’t mind paying for), and while it helped me collect in-app currency faster, I’ve started to feel less motivated because there’s not much I’m excited to spend it on. Most of the furniture and outfits feel repetitive—lots of similar items in different colors—and I rarely find something new or interesting for my bird. It feels like I’m seeing the same few options over and over again, which takes away from that sense of progress.

I know there’s a much bigger catalog of items that might become available in the future, but with only a handful of new items shown each day, it can feel like a long wait without much payoff.

That said, I really appreciate what Finch is doing. It’s helped me build momentum when nothing else was working. I just hope future updates make the reward system feel a bit more exciting and dynamic for long-term users.

title: Love it, even after 3 years.
body:
2025 update
Still using the app almost daily. I have paid for the full version and have zero regrets. It’s actually the only app I’ve ever paid for and it’s been worth it. It’s around $5 month when you break it down and that is far cheaper than therapy and executive function coach. If one is to use the app for maximum benefit that is in reflecting and observing your experience through different moments and situations. Don’t get distracted by special events if you don’t want (they give the option to turn that off) and keep up with the journal aspects and that’s where you get the true mental health clarity and help. Task tracking is fun and easy, can be scheduled or just a giant list. There are so many ways they have given choices to user to make each flavour of brain and struggle to have choice and control. I really applaud their amazing efforts. Some aspects haven’t been my favourite but that’s ok, because over all it has truly helped me.
You can bring your mood tracker to medical appointments to help show up and downs, you can create hashtags to track medications or other formal treatments also to aid in conversations and evidence for medical team to review impacts over weeks or even time of day. I have found it to be both personally helpful and my doctor has also found it to be helpful and asks to see regularity during appointments. 

Can’t find my old review, I like to update it as I use the app, I’m still using it 3 years later. My doctor loves how the calendar can help track symptoms and moods, I love being able to track productive days vs low energy days. My young kiddo uses it also, we both use the breathing exercises and grounding exercises. Love it.

If you mark your motivation or mood low it offers a check in and you end up doing a mini reflection session that is super helpful. I’m on an 109 day streak right now. I told my therapist about it and they’ve added it to their suggested resources.

title: 5/5 but sharing some feature wishes !
body:
I have ADHD and this app is saving my life. Incredibly grateful for it. Got the free version and considering paying for it eventually, to unlock all the exercises (breathing & exercise) and to support an app that’s so helpful to me. Love how the free version is enough to be helpful forever and the paid stuff is just a bonus. Hope it always stays that way. 

Feature wishes regarding the focus timer:
- I wish there was an option to make the timer stop if I get off the app, to prevent me from being on my phone during work time
- I wish there was an option to start a shared timer with a friend ! « Peer pressure » helps me and I’d feel bad goofing off if I know my friend is hard at work. 

Thank you 1000x for this lovely app, I talk about it so much that people must think they’re sponsoring me 😂

title: I don’t think self care apps should do that
body: When I had Finch the first time I hatched a green birb named “Keg!” I got it to full grown and spent more and more time with the bird getting emotionally attached to the birb and his home, After a while I slowed down with how much I went on the app. one night I realized that I had forgotten to send him on an adventure that day and when I went onto finch to check on him I got got a pop up from finch on my screen that said they had “lost my birb” and tried to make it up to me by giving me 5000 gems, a new birb and I still had all the stuff I got for Keg! This had a horrible impact on my mental heath. I gave up on finch for a while. After a bit I came back to finch to give it another shot, this time I hatched a birb named “Kirin” when I hatched kirin I made sure to be extra careful with him I made sure to backup his file and even put a task on my finch board for every once in a while to make sure the file was good. I got kirin to about a week away from becoming an adult when my phone broke when I got a new phone and redownloaded finch Kirin was still there but he had been sent almost all the way back to the start of child with all of the stuff I had gotten for him since then missing. I personally won’t be trusting finch again anytime soon while I had it the first time I enjoyed it, when I had it the second time I enjoyed it but was constantly concerned about them loosing my birb.

It's a wellness app, encouraging you to complete goals. Take care of you, even the little things, life gets so busy. Finch is there to guide you every step of the way. You get a bird that you can dress up, get lil pets and travel along the way. Super motivational. Inclusive to all genders/ disabilities. The community around finch and users are wonderful. 

I recommend to everyone mental health struggles or not. Everyone should have wellness. 

Kudos to the developers who created this app. constantly updating making it better(which was not thought possible) , taking suggestions. Making it safe for everyone, as catering to all ages can be difficult. 
The team go above and beyond, Super grateful. Proud user and support of finch!

title: Life-Changing App for Motivation and Self-Esteem
body:
Since becoming jobless and struggling with feeling like there’s no purpose to get up in the morning, Finch has truly transformed my day-to-day life. This app has become an incredible tool for boosting my self-esteem and motivation, helping me feel good about myself again. It encourages me to complete simple tasks like getting out of bed, brushing my teeth, and taking a few deep breaths — all of which are checked off as achievements. Each task I complete, no matter how small, helps me feel productive and proud of myself.

The app’s cute characters and the daily motivational quotes they share are such a wonderful touch. They’ve genuinely made me feel loved and supported, even on days when it’s tough to get going. Over time, I’ve set more challenging goals for myself, like doing yoga daily, and the app rewards me with a cute little prize every time I accomplish these harder tasks.

Finch has been a godsend not only for me but for my entire family. My daughter, husband, and even my friends have joined in, and we support each other by sending reminders, affirmations, and daily pick-me-ups. The ability to send gifts and hold each other accountable has been so helpful. We’ve created a supportive community where we all encourage each other to stay on track with our tasks, big or small. Even when I was sick last week, I still managed to get up and complete my tasks, thanks to the gentle motivation Finch provides.

I’m truly grateful for this app. If you’re looking for a way to stay motivated and tackle daily tasks, I highly recommend giving Finch a try. It’s a free app that’s made a huge difference in my life, and I’m confident it can help you too.

My only issue is a small nit picky thing- i get notifications that say "i'm feeling loved. How are you feeling?" title: Fabulous for kids and adults alike!
body:
What a great concept for a self care app. 

My nephew recently got a new phone and was excited about finding this app. He asked me to be his friend on it and I figured, why not, reminded me of a tamogotchi back in the day.. and I love taking any opportunity to engage with him. 

Well… let me tell you. As an adult with late-diagnosed ADHD, this app has been a game changer for building consistency in the little habits of life. I love that I find myself naturally doing these little (big to my brain) tasks that felt so dreaded previously… and if I don’t, I check in and voila I’m reminded! 🙂

Truly, love that they’ve made the real self care super fun and engaging for the younger generations.. 

I do wish they’d make it so you could sort your goals by time, it would help me visualize and scan for missed tasks more easily… but hey, that’s my only “complaint” cause otherwise I’m a big fan! 

Well done! 🙌🙌🙌

title: Fun and cute but kind of useless if you enjoy lying and hate sentimentality
body:
This is NOT is a design flaw on the part of the devs, as I’m sure it’s very effective for its core audience (people invested in the concept of self-care and take gamification at face value) but this is a warning to people who are resistant to habit-building, don’t get any intrinsic reward from ticking things off a list, and are not emotionally moved by virtual pets: this app is not for us. It’s a solid app! I’m sure it’s helped lots of people! But I would not recommend this app to people who are going to realize that you can just lie to your digital child about the things you did that day. I also just kind of find it strange that your allegedly-adult Finch will gush about things like The Very Hungry Caterpillar and milk like they’re finding out these things exist for the first time.

Once again: as an app, it is good, hence the four stars. I write this review as a caution for people who think their treatment-resistant brain will be fixed by an app: it will not. It will just be a dress-up game for you, which is also fine, but not what it’s meant for.

title: Very helpful
body:
If it were just a matter that this app helps me organize tasks and chores day to day while raising and taking care of a cute bird the grows and learns along the way I would give this app 5 stars. It does so much more though, it provides a number of tools that can help when dealing with emotional and mental turmoil with grounding techniques and breathing exercises. Finch has options to reflect on different things that may be affecting me day to day allowing for deeper dives into exploring why certain emotions come up when dealing with situations that can be causing internal turmoil. I have found I’m even able to effectively and comfortably journal my emotional state day to day as well, while keeping track of how I’m doing at a given time when checking in with my little finch. I have definitely found this app provides some excellent features that have helped me in ways I honestly never thought I would get from an app.

It’s not a replacement for therapy but it has helped act as a bandaid when I am struggling day to day and need to find calm and grounding in a moment.

If you want to use the app to help with choirs it’s excellent for that. If you need something that helps with mindfulness and reflection this app is great for that too.

title: Best thing I’ve done to improve productivity.
body:
I have never been one to stick with any kind of productivity app or have much success creating new good habits. This app changed that for me. It is so incredibly well done. You get the satisfaction of checking something off your to-do list, but get the added bonus of a reward. I have also never been one to journal, write reflections or make note of things I’m grateful for. This app allows you to do as little or as much of that as you like, and it has felt really good to kind of microdose those things with the option to do more if I want. I love that you can connect with friends, but there’s no actual direct messaging. Having to answer messages can feel like a mental burden sometimes, so I like that it doesn’t just turn into another social media app. I feel like there is so much more I could say but I 10/10 recommend trying this app if you are looking for ways to create new positive habits or just be more productive.

*One feature I would love to see added to the app is an undo button when changing outfits for furniture. If, for instance, I try a new hat and don’t like it, I hate having to scroll all the way back through my inventory to put the hat I was just wearing back on.

Keep up the great works devs!

I know i don’t “have to”, but it feels like added pressure, and something - even though inanimate - that I’m responsible for.  My life is exceptionally busy - work has “slowed down” to about 40 hours/week over winter, and i have other things i need to do with any free time as well. I don’t want the added pressure of feeling like I’m failing if i don’t spend time with my bird…if this makes sense?  I don’t remember that it was always like that…

author: Finch🪽

title: ADHD, Depression, even CPTSD help?! (And it’s so stinking cute, too!)
body:
I have NEVER stuck to any goal-tracking apps, although I have tried MANY. (Looking for apps to help with ADHD but too ADHD to stick to it…)

This one though? I started using this app 54 days ago, and I know this because I’m on my 54th day streak?! The app is amazing, it really works for me. 

For anyone with depression: I recommend dragging a couple of friends to your friend tree because “sending good vibes” from your smol birb to theirs really helps to break isolation.

For anyone with ADHD: The app has a feature to add a screen widget- I actually picked the biggest possible widget that takes half my phone screen and slapped it on there. Now I see my adorable birb instead of any social apps and always check in with her! It has worked!

For anyone with CPTSD from childhood trauma: This app may even help to heal some old wounds that you didn’t know you had. Your baby birb will grow up as they go on adventures, and they come back with a “discovery” at the end of each of these. You are offered choices that can reassure them, empower them or otherwise help them understand this whole new world they are exploring. Making my birb feel safe in her own personality and in her own experiences has helped me cope with the lack of similar support from my own parental figures. It is surprisingly healing, I did not expect that at all from a virtual “pet” app… But it’s just so much more than that.

A big thank you to the Finch team for bringing this app to us!

title: Streak breaks
body:
This is a good & cute motivational app, but every time I've missed a day, it was because I spent the time taking care of myself and enjoying the day. But when I log in the next day, I see I missed my chance to log the goals I reached. I can't reap the rewards of my success. I can't even acknowledge that they happened. Goals don't show up at all for that specific day you missed.

And I find that really frustrating. I'm usually really good at checking in, but I'm being punished for the days I do extra well. I can't imagine it feels good the other way either. If you have a really bad day and can barely force yourself to reach any of your goals, you can't even go back to acknowledge those small successes you did manage to have. I understand the point of streaks overall, but in this case, there's some downsides to it, that I'd like to see addressed.

title: Helped me so much!
body:
I tried this app in it’s earlier stages but didn’t stick with it cause I now know I was using it wrong! I was just putting my to do list in there and not even focusing on the self-care part🫣 

I am better at taking my medication, cleanliness, hygiene, happiness!!! I go to therapy and truly had a hard time remembering techniques to use in moments of need but the app has a “First Aid Kit” that has so many different ways to help in a jiff!

I’ve told so many people about this app and they started telling their people, I also got my therapist on the app and now they’re telling other clients and people in their life.

Truly so grateful for this app, I really didn’t even mention all the cool stuff they offer: 
Cute customizable bird pet, pets for your pet, customizable room, add friends and send them encouragement (no chat room), you can travel and learn about new places, add as many goals as you need/want, can turn off the streak counter, great for really any age that needs to boost, monthly gifts, you can sponsor someone to have a free membership which is really just to unlock a few extra clothing and furniture items but the whole app can be used free *pretty sure* Membership isn’t going to break the bank for those who can afford it.

The creators are constantly working with the users to figure out what works and what doesn’t, communication is wildly amazing for the small team.

Not sure what else I can about how awesome this app is and the people who created it! Love it and truly thank you❤️❤️❤️❤️

title: Tomogachi for adults
body:
My co worker showed me this app just a few days ago and it’s truly incredible. For those with ADHD especially (or audhd) I highly recommend this app as although to some it may seem silly to need. Clearly it isn’t made for them! This app gives you those small victories throughout the day and wonderful reminders. I have just started using it and excited to continue it. My boyfriend also downloaded the app and we are both very much enjoying our birbs so far!

From reminders for self care like drink water (I am very bad at that one) to daily medication or work reminders, ect… it has changed the game for taking care of you! YOU are the tomogachi and yes some could say just create fake goals or could “cheat” but that defeats the purpose of this app. I am definitely going to purchase the yearly when I can. I saw there were some options for cost wise. I’m only working part time currently so will be choosing the lighter payment option however if and when I do have better funds, I very much would love to contribute to this app. Incredible!

title: THE BEST!!!
body: Finch is SUCH an awesome app, it’s good for all ages, it’s cute, and it makes you actually WANT to do stuff because there’s rewards. There are SO MANY amazing features, but since I can’t list them all, I’ll just say a few of my favourites. (I will definitely forget some but oh well.) Friends feature: hang out with friends, send good vibes, request a hug (it’s so nice to have support ☺️); outfit feature: gained as rewards or bought through the shop (all in game money, earned from doing things!); journeys feature: group of quests from selection or self made, special journey milestones and rewards as well; the sheer simplicity of it all: buttons are clear, they pop up a little, if you forgot where something is it won’t take long to find it; mental and physical health: this app is all about health without being patronizing or annoying about it, there’s a first aid kid with calming strategies and a help line, there’s disorder quizzes, it helps you narrow down your feelings; breathing and calm: there’s lots of different breathing exercises, and they all work! There’s calm, winding down, energy, and more! Ok, there’s definitely a WHOLE lot more to Finch like discoveries and your pet finch (which I’m just now realizing that i didn’t really talk about 😅) but you’ll have to discover it for yourself! A friend recommended me this app, and since i got it it is part of my hourly life, as I’ve said it is just so amazing, and i know that it has seriously helped a lot of project people. As a quick little warning, yes there is finch plus, with locked features, so some of you might be annoyed by that, but none of the cute things are locked, it’s more like adding extra stuff you don’t actually NEED it, y’know? Ok, if you’ve made it this far, congratulations! I know that was a lot, sorry. I wholeheartedly recommend this app to literally anyone, it doesn’t matter if you’re not struggling or don’t necessarily need it, it’s awesome. Thank you so much Finch, bye everyone!

title: Can only get better!
body:
Hi finch team!

I’ve been using finch for over a month now, and I’ve never missed a day since downloading. I love how kind and gentle it is. I appreciate that I can set simple goals, and by accomplishing only a few I can send Pickles (my finch) on a cute little adventure. All the quotes and positive messages make me feel lighter and see myself through kinder eyes when I don’t complete all my goals. I still feel accomplished even on my worse days. 

My only feedback is that I’d love a way to fly back to maps id already started exploring, and maybe didn’t finish. when I first met Sassafras and traveled, I thought it was part of the tutorial and assumed I could go back to finch forest and finish exploring there. 

I like to 100% simple games like these, I find it a fun aspect especially when it takes a long time to achieve it. I’d even be willing to pay 500 Rainbow stones (or something) to do it. I’d like to be able to hop around 2 or 3 at a time, to keep my adhd brain engaged. 

Seriously tho- it’s a great app. Thank you for making accessibly for everyone two. I deeply appreciate how great the impacts been even though I can’t pay for the premium. You creators rock, and I hope other in the industry take note. ❤️

title: Finally, a habit tracker that loves my ADHD!
body:
Listen, I’m no expert and this is just from my own experience; but what I can tell you is that after more than 30 years of trying and failing to set and keep good habits, Finch has made it fun enough for this chronic procrastinator to stick to it for over 150 days.

That’s 150 days of checking in with myself. Not necessarily checking everything off of my list, but at least taking the time to assess what I did and didn’t do for myself that day, and why.

And honestly? That’s something I’d never been able to do before. This app made it fun. It’s helped me build everything that goes around good habits: self trust, curiosity, routine, reward. 

Plus, it’s adorable and I’ve definitely gotten attached to my little bird.

If you’re the kind of person who struggles with what seems to come naturally to those around you, Finch might help. 

You can just do it lightheartedly, by keeping it simple and collecting items and points; or you can dig deep with reflections and by looking at these detailed reports of your activities that they compile for you. Either way, it’s a self-care Neopet, and who wouldn’t love that? 🤷‍♀️

By the way: it’s just as fun without the paid membership. I finally caved and got the membership after about half a year, just for extra items, but you really can enjoy it without.

Cheers, Finch team! You folks rock and I hope you’re proud of your work. ❤️

I saw an ad for it on instagram and I can’t tell you how perfect the timing was. I had just been feeling like my overall stability was slipping lately and so I decided to redownload it! I was worried it might have become a paid subscription only app as most health and self care apps have become lately but I was happy to see that so much is available for free. Enough to make a difference! And never a single ad <3 You can just tell that this was created by people that really care about the impact they have on their user. They do not limit the free users the way other apps do. They’re generous and have created a seemingly small but powerful and accessible tool. title: Engaging, not distracting.
body:
Finch gamifies self-care in a way that keeps me coming back every day without becoming another unhealthy distraction on my phone. Perfect for people that thrive on to-do lists, with the added bonus of a sweet little dopamine hit with every item you check off. Adding little habits that are already a regular part of your daily routine is a helpful reminder that you’re doing great even on harder days where loftier goals are tougher to meet.

 The art and writing are so endearing, and having a digital pet attached to my self-care journey is a small, adorable motivator that helps me on harder days. All in all a wonderful app. 🥰

title: Another good app ruined with a streak function
body:
I really really loved this app, it has a great message and amazing supports and has really made me feel like I’m building good habits. Recently there was an update that added the streak function as something that is way more prominent, the first thing that pops up when you open the app and it has made me really hate going there. Some days I get super busy and my memory issues are much worse and I forget to log into finch to check off my progress. It happens. Before this streak update it wasn’t so prominent and genuinely made me feel like not checking in for a day was a minor thing and didn’t make me feel disappointed in myself. I dread going into finch because of this new feature and I’m just gutted because I really loved this app and have noticed better mental health because of it. 

I have lost my streak twice since the new update and it makes me so angry and sad and frustrated that I have to spend all my coins to regain my streak. Now that it pops up every time I open the app it’s just a reminder that I feel like a failure because my memory which is impacted by my mental health and disability is the reason that number should be higher. It really makes me feel like a failure not going in every day now that this streak update has happened and the first time I lost my streak I paid all my coins and the second time has just made me want to uninstall the app. 

This app was just amazing, with so many great features to support my mental health journey and I genuinely feel like it has been ruined with this new prominence of the streak. This feature is so discouraging and in my opinion should not be included. This has been a huge let down for me as I really love going in and seeing my improvements and considering this is an app focused on mental health why is penalizing users who very often have difficulty forming healthy habits a feature????

title: I didn’t even know how much this would help.
body: After diagnoses, medication and therapy have been helping a lot, but I still struggle with so many things. I kept seeing IG ads for this, and wasn’t super into the pet part, but decided to give it a look. Within a week I was talking it up to pretty much everyone I know. I struggle so much with executive dysfunction and getting started, and having the list of goals, small doable items I usually put off, habits I have never started, with me all the time, no pressure or guilt if I don’t do them, sorted by the things that are important to me to remind me why, in an app designed to be interesting but not to keep you in it, but loop you back to the reel world, with short, accessible and doable therapy, exercise, breath bits, and a complete lack of predatory structure (want to impulse purchase a thing for your nest? Then save, sell, or complete goals because there is no easy ‘spend real money for fake money’ option). The extras in the subscription are really extras - all the core function is in the free version. I have been using this app for almost a month, and I plan to celebrate at a month by subscribing, not because there is anything holding me back in the free version, but because I really want to support this amazing resource.

title: Useful, Fun & SUPER Cute!
body:
I’ve tried many self-care apps before and most of them didn’t really have much of an incentive for checking in. But with Finch, I have a little birb to take care of and the things I do in my life helps them in theirs. I love sending my birb on her daily adventures and hearing about her discoveries. I think being able to decorate the house and dress them up is also such a great way to motivate me to check off my daily goals.

What I think is a really neat choice is how, when hatching micro-pets, you have to do that goal for 7 days in a row for it to actually hatch. It’s not a thing you do quickly, you have to nurture it like you would nurture your own habits and then, when it hatches, the pay-off is so much better and satisfying than if it happened the same day.

The free version has enough to support yourself and the premium version is definitely a plus, but it’s not needed. Other apps ask you to subscribe or pay to even use them, but Finch recognizes that mental health care should be accessible. This is also evidenced by the Guardian system and I think that is just such a beautiful thing.

Finch, keep doing whatever you’re doing because it’s working! I love my birb and seeing her every day. It helps me feel better about myself and helps me to take care of myself. My search for the perfect self-care/mental health app is finally over!

title: so much more than a self care app with a pet
body:
When I was recommended the Finch app by my friend, I thought it would be just a self care app that rewarded me for taking caring of myself with my pet staying alive like a tamagotchi. 

The app is actually wonderful and supporting and has so many tools available and goals you can set for things you didn't realize you needed. 

The app has sleep aids, healthy body and healthy eating goals, breathing exercises, mental health resources - you can set as many or as few goals as you like. 

I really recommend the app just for helping you love yourself, helping you reflect and grow about things in your day to day life - it is genuinely the best self care app I've seen - because they provide everything you could need for your mental and physical health in a loving way. 

Not to mention it helps you appreciate yourself and your body and your friendships.

title: Not enjoying the new direction…
body: I’ve been using this app for over 500 days now and have been a sponsor for nearly as long. It’s become a part of my daily routine and I’ve regarded it highly enough that I’ve been willing to pay extra so others can access it. I can’t say I like the new direction the app is taking though. Having gambling machine sounds when gems are acquired is just unpleasant and isn’t a great thought to bring to mind. Now the app is tracking “streaks” and asking players to pay gems to get their “streaks” back. The “carrot” is what worked with Finch, it was a supportive, open, shame-free environment built on the idea of a micro pet that loved and believed in the user unconditionally. Bringing in the “stick” of tracking the user for missed days and prompting them to pay to erase the mistake with gains they’ve made by actually meeting their goals runs counter to what made the app great.

title: A fun way to do chores
body:
I’m so glad they have a free version because I’m on disability and couldn’t afford anything else.

This is perfect for anyone who’s neurodivergent. There’s a maximum number of tasks you can add to your list (which means I’m not setting myself up for failure before I even have breakfast).

There’s a help section with options ranging from breathing to straight up CBT. And there’s your finch.

Right at the beginning you hatch your own finch, you pick their colour, name, and pronouns then you set them out to adventure. Every task you complete helps them grow and gives you rainbow gems to buy them clothes and decorate their home.

It’s a peaceful, entertaining, and rewarding way to do chores.

title: Pleasantly Surprised
body:
I saw this ad on social media and thought I would see what it was all about. I expected it to be very superficial and assumed the content would be very surface level, not motivating and would make me feel like a failure when I wasn’t able to actually complete the tasks. 

I was wrong.

I look forward to popping on and seeing my little pet and I’m invested in keeping my streak. There is the option to both create your own goals or to use ones they have suggested and even on the free version there is no shortage of SO many choices - attainable ones. It’s a wide variety of things as simple as getting out of bed, or taking a drink of water or can support you with larger goals like being involved in your community. 

Aside from the daily tasks that you can list there is a section called “journeys” and this basically allows you to identify a goal (again, choose from their options or create your own) and add multiple “smaller” goals/tasks to ultimately contribute to your goal. My favourite right now is the tidy journey; prompts to help clean again starting small and simple or the bigger tasks. 

What I love most is that this is labelled as a JOURNEY, it is something you can work on when you’re able to for as long as you need to. You can select reminders, repetition, snoozing, adding additional goals or removing them. They also have journeys to help during anxiety attacks with breathing, sounds, observations and other therapeutic tools and reward you for those too! 

I wish there was a monthly payment plan as a full year is a lot up front and while I hope to still be as diligent in a year - my track record isn’t great. For now I’m enjoying the free tools and resources provided and there are AMPLE!

Glad I tried :)

title: Corny but works so well
body:
First.  It is very well-made, solid professional app that is all encompassing.  

Second. It has a wide variety of self help/care angles.  Things I’d not think to try like breathing exercises or a reflection on my “triggers”.  I would not have gotten an app for that but since they are features I tried it, and have felt the benefits.   The Finch may be considered corny but it works.  I had never brush my teeth twice a day for any amount of days in a row and now, I don’t miss it, cause I want my micro pet.  I laugh at myself for loving it so much.

I am grateful to the developers for this app . I am getting better .  This app is worth the money.

title: So cute and motivating
body: I’ve tried other habit trackers — even gamified ones — before, but they never really stuck for me. A lot of them leave you feeling stressed out or guilty when you don’t hit all your goals. Finch is really working for me so far, though: it’s all carrot and no stick (ie: all reward, no punishment), which is what I tend to need. You’re gently encouraged by your sweet little finch friend, the sound effects are soothing and satisfying, and there’s no punishment or guilting for not completing some of your goals: if you don’t complete them, you just don’t collect the gems for those goals yet, which is fine. There’s always tomorrow! Everything in the game is super cute, and I do find myself finding more ways to improve my self-care just for the excuse to spend a few extra minutes here and there with my little finch. 💖
author: Nikki Scarlet

title: I love it
body: I saw an ad for this on insta, didn’t expect it to be especially helpful but I was curious. After trying it out for a few days I found myself being much more productive and it’s made me proud of how much I’m able to get done. I have adhd and anxiety, tasks slip my mind easily and everything can seem overwhelming at times. But to have a list that shows all of my daily chores, and to be able to add whatever else needs to be done that day, and to have a sense of accomplishment when checking something off my list is surprisingly helpful. The positive dopamine boost when I get points, receive gifts etc. it even rewards you for listening to relaxing background audio, journaling, anxiety management exercises etc. I can’t believe how helpful this has been for me. It’s so simple yet effective. I’m very grateful to whoever created this app, it’s made my tasks much more manageable. Thank you so much

title: I was having so much fun with this app, then the game glitched & erased my bird
body:
It started when for some reason anytime I tried to write a reflection, the app would crash. Weird but I thought maybe it couldn’t handle writing too much. Then one day I opened the app on Monday and for some reason a goal I put in had duplicated itself like 500 times, causing the app to lag and crash after a few minutes. This would happen every Monday as the goal was set to renew then, and I couldn’t find a way to fix it.

Today was no exception. I opened the app and tried to ‘complete’ as many of the duplicate missions as quickly as I could to get rid of them between crashes, and then I opened it and… got a message saying my pet data was corrupted and my bird would have to be rehatched. All the time spent completing Tokyo, all the unique decorations I got by subscribing to Finch Plus… my bird’s unique personality, it was all gone, just like that. I’m heartbroken. I don’t want to start over with a new bird, I want my Açai back.

Suggestions to improve App: Add a button to read out the task - Allow family members to link (siblings) and allow parents to add tasks and view completed tasks on another device (a family subscription) - add more of a variety of exercises (maybe some yoga poses). We are still exploring this App and will give more feedback. Thanks 😀

title: Finch has lasted me over a month

I like how the focus timers give you points too… the only improvements I feel would REALLY help me would be custom timer options, alarm clock, and the ability to tie timers to goals - ex. You can start a 30 min timer and write in that it’s for a particular task. Also being able to start another activity in the same day would be nice. I love the positivity and all the cute stuff - it’s been making my life a bit better recently, and I needed that. Thank you Finch! (And the guardians!)

title: Feel Better with Finch
body:
I have suggested this to my own counsellors as well as to numerous colleagues and friends I am a registered Social Worker in Alberta Canada and a child and youth care worker. I also struggle with depression, anxiety  and as a woman late diagnosed significant inattentive ADHD i have my whole life I am a survivor of severe childhood trauma  hence working in the helping fields recently I have had three super close significant losses in my life and I have fallen into a hole but Finch honestly is so cute and I have a full tree of support sometimes you forget they are there I love sending them positive messages every day numerous times a day I believe it builds resiliency I love the game aspect for working on goals that help you be more successful and that there is a work- life balance involved I’m on that journey now. I never knew I needed it so much until I started on finch and it reminded me to reflect the reflection parts are very helpful and there is no set limits. 

That’s really the basis of Finch to take care of yourself to use many aspects of self care from standing up for just 10 seconds on rough days to helping others in days it’s rough. When you take care of your basic needs and mental health I was surprised how without noticing it  other aspects of my life improved. Finch reminds you your amazing and  how to look for the good when you are surrounded by pain and darkness. It not a cure all but it reminds you to work to be healthier and to take care of yourself while normalizing that’s okay. Yep one little bird and a tree with bird friends helped me see the sun more it’s still a work in progress but life is a journey not a destination so enjoy the walk it doesn’t have to be a treacherous hike all the time

title: Dear Finch Team
body:
Dear Finch Care Team,

I have been an active user of Finch since August 23rd - downloading this app was the best thing I have done to help me with my wellness journey. This app helps me track my moods, gives me a place to rant, keeps me on track with mindfulness, managing anxiety, daily activities and tasks and so much more. 
Last month I was chosen to be sponsored by a guardian, having access to finch plus was great. I was able to do extra things to help me with everything listed above, it also added a lot of fun to my experience by getting all the special rewards. I knew that my sponsorship would likely be coming to an end this month but to my surprise when I clicked that I couldn’t afford the plan, I was again gifted Finch plus for free. I literally said “wow, no way!” out loud. It made me feel so special and loved knowing that the creators of this app actually really care about me. 
Thank you, from the bottom of my heart. 

Love, Olivia & my Finch Cutie ❤️

title: Seriously can’t recommend this enough.
body: Ive tried so many goal/self-care/planning/mood apps through the years but have never stuck with one. I always used it for a few days and forgot about it. For context, I’m some random 23 year old university graduate trying to sort her life out. Finch is so incredible. I’ve gotten 2 of my friends to use it too- they love it. The shopping element (decorating your bird and its home) is the biggest thing for me. That aspect is really fun- but most importantly you pay using gems you can only earn by using the app (setting/compelting goals, answering prompts to process thoughts/emotions). Aka- you can’t use real money. So, I’m encouraged to use the self-care features because it’s the only way to buy the cute items (and I really want them lol). B/c of that, I’m doing stuff like trying some guided anxiety management journey which I had no interest in doing before (you get soo many gems if you complete it). It’s nothing too special, just stuff like “listen to this soundscape for 10 minutes”, but those small actions can have a big impact on us! I just think the app developers used some psychology principles to guide them with certain features- and it really pays off!! I highly highly highly suggest trying this out!! It’s not for everyone, just like how those other apps I tried weren’t for me, but if it IS for you, you’re going to be obsessed!

title: Literally life changing
body:
Ok, so I want to start off by saying this app is no replacement for professional mental health care
However, as someone who has struggled with their mental health for well over half of my life- it is an AMAZING tool. 
It has kept me on track so I do not allow myself to fully spiral nearly as often, and stay consistent in life and through my appointments with basic care that I struggle so hard with.
Premium is amazing if you can afford it, additionally there are sponsorships for some who can't 
The fact it's designed as an adorable bird as well- it activates my compulsive caring must take care of others mode that seems to come with depression. 
Idk I'm just really impressed, this app was well thought out, designed, and while there are others similar, this one is the only one I've been able to stick with consistently, I hit 250 days today.

Thank you y'all

title: LOVE, but feel there are missed opportunities
body:
I’m absolutely loving this app, I’m sharing it with everybody, because it’s been life changing for me, but I have some ideas that I think many people would benefit from. 

While sharing I’ve noticed that adding friends is a little finicky eg; when I share my friend code and someone signs up the only way I know is through a notification… but if I accidentally clear that notification there’s no way to redeem the reward in app. I have to go back to the text I sent them - click the invite text - then get redirected back to the app where it then prompts me to redeem the invite reward. After the other person has activated their Finch account they can send me high-fives etc, but I can’t send it to them unless we have each others friend codes… and there’s no friend list besides the Tree Town (which is very cute). Another odd thing about this is people can add me through friend code but I can’t add them? an example of this; I shared the app with my sister, who then shared it with my niece. My niece got my friend code from my sister and sent me a little hug and I was able to send her a little dance break back, but there was no prompt to add her like I feel there should have been. 

I also think it would be really neat to have multiple types of “Tree Towns”. I’ve been sharing this app with my coworkers (we’re all stressed out baristas who are mostly neurodiverse lol), and I’d love to add them all, but it feels a bit weird to my brain to have coworkers I don’t typically interact with outside of work mixed in with my family and significant others. Maybe that’s just me tho! Just an idea ;) 

What I would most love to see though, is to be able to share “journeys” with other users (roommates, partners, siblings etc). I think it would be really cute to do this by adding a sort of “coparenting” feature where you raise a second finch with someone. I’d love to be able to use the app to organize every day tasks with my partner - like taking turns cooking meals, household chores that we struggle to do regularly etc. We could also use it to help build new habits, like reading books together or learning a new language (partnership w duolingo? i’m just daydreaming now lol). I think this could also be really helpful for support workers to check-in and work alongside the people they help, parents could also help kids with building habits, or even for recovering addicts who need someone to stay accountable to in low stress way? The ways this could help in terms of motivation & accountability are endless! 

Bottom line - THIS APP IS FANTASTIC. It may seem like I’m focusing on what this app doesn’t do, but really I’m just inspired by all it can/ could do! The ways this app can be utilized - all while being super freaking cute, focused on accessibility, and while having an awesome UI.. it’s amazing. I’ve tried so many apps and this one is the best, Thank you Nino & Steph! 🫶

The next time I opened the app, it appeared as if I never won or accepted anything with no information whatsoever about what I had won. I contacted finch and they said there was nothing they could no to fix it and the app did it on its own. It’s a shame because the app is really good at helping manage my anxiety and depression, but I now feel triggered from just using the app. My brother passed away recently and I was hoping to have an app help with my mental health while going through this, not an app that causes more stress.

i rarely ever review apps, but i feel like this app is a must. this might sound like a bit typinf but it’s not. this app used to be a big thing for me and my friends back in 2021. most of the group split apart aside from me and my friend, i’ll call him beau. beau and i have been friends since the summer of 2021. during late 2021 early 2022, we found an app called finch. this was a pretty big thing in our small group at the time, everyday we would log into the app, send everyone a get well message and complete all our tasks, we had matching finch names and outfits, and we were the closest we ever were at that point.
