title: Finch turns self care into a game!
body:
I’ve always had trouble with self care, and most apps don’t help me to stay on track. This is the first app that I’ve been able to use for a whole month, and I’ve seen genuine improvement! I highly recommend this app if you struggle with self care, and even if you don’t, it’s still nice to be rewarded for your efforts.

Pros:
- You care for your finch by caring for yourself! No worries about making sure they’re fed or anything.
- You can pet the bird!!!
- You can customize your finch, their clothing, and even their house! You get more customization options as they grow.
- They can even have a pet of their own!
- Every task you set and complete will energize your finch, and gives you in-game currency.
- Once your finch is energized, they can go on an adventure! They’ll come back and talk to you about it.
- Those adventures take time, but that time goes down quicker with each task you complete.
- From my understanding, every month has a new season of items and rewards that you get just for sending your finch on an adventure. Items come back in the shop randomly!
- No micro-transactions. The only thing you can buy is a subscription that unlocks more items to customize with, but Finch is generous enough to give you free trials as an occasional reward, and they even have a system in place where community members might give you a month-long subscription.
- You can encourage your friends who also have Finch, and they can do the same!
- The app will ask how you’re doing every now and then, and if you say you aren’t doing well, it recommends ways of dealing with that and little first aid options to calm yourself.
- All your tasks and things you write are private; it only saves things to keep track of your well-being, and you’re the only one that sees it.

Cons:
- My only gripe is that I wish there was more to do in the app that focuses on your finch. I love the customization and that they talk to you every now and then, but I’d love to see more ways to interact with them. I’ve been using this for a month, so there might be more options in the future!

title: LOVE THIS APP + ideas for updates
body:
This app is amazing! I have been using it on and off for a while but lately I’m obsessed. I love adding my goals and completing them to gain xp like a video game! 

One idea I have. I think you should be able to have more than one finch. It could be presented in different ways such as : once your finch is an adult they have an egg of their own, giving them a baby. Or just on a different section of the app you can select another finch to take care of. That way if one of your finches is adventuring, you can still take care of one. 

Another thing I’d like to have added :
 
Daily tasks to take care of you finch. Such as if you have a basic goal like “eat a nutritious breakfast” then you can also select some food for your finch so they can eat with you. As well, I think it’d be cool if your finch can go in their bed when it’s your set sleeping time and you can say goodnight with your finch. 

I love this app and it’s really helped me! I hope the developers take my ideas into consideration while making their well though our updates. Thank you for reading.  -Mila and my finch child Chowder.

title: I recommend it to all my friends!
body: I usually get apps like this, use it for a month maybe and then never open it again. My little finch is so cute and personally it motivates me to go check in on her every day and in doing so I check in with myself. They grow and change and each time you interact a new part of their personality develops. You can earn friend ship points and you get sweet little messages through out the day if you enable notifications. I have been active on finch nearly every day for a year and have noticed an improvement in my mental health for sure. I recently decided to upgrade to the plus option to support the company after being so happy with the app. When you complete goals or do check ins you  earn coins and can use them to get things for your finch like house decor, clothes and even plane tickets to go on adventures. I also liked that you had access to so many features even if you use the free app and not the upgraded (finch plus). My sister also has the app and lives abroad. It’s so sweet that Because we are ‘neighbours’ we can send each other things like ‘high fives’ and ‘gratefulness’ and our finch’s come to visit each other. Super cute and over all really happy with it!

title: For you and your loved ones.
body:
This is the best app for working on yourself through a slump or rough time. It encourages you to take those small self care steps in the kindest cutest way possible. There’s so much more than a checklist, you fall in love with your birb and don’t want to let them down, and you never will. I have my mom and sister on the app with me and my mom is extremely consistent. I love seeing her birb pop up to send me love and spend time with mine. I love getting to know my birb and I love dressing and decorating. Most of all I love that it helps me. The developers truly care about the users it’s not a money grab even remotely. They have so much in place for free users and so many affordable options for the premium. Both are beyond worth what they cost.

Thank you so much for making this app. You are helping so many people and the love you’ve created, the motivation and the help to keep us dedicated is more than anyone could ask from an app. 

With so much love and sincerity, if you think you might want this app… try it.

title: Adorable has a lot of care put into it
body:
The thing that sets this app apart is that a lot of the self care help is absolutely free. 

They have grounding techniques, breathing exercises and so much more for you to utilize in helping you learn to take care of yourself and I love that. 

I am also so grateful that the social aspect is not behind a pay wall either. It’s so nice to be able to send some good vibes to my friends and let them know I’m thinking about them and vice versa.

It’s clear the developers really believe in what they are doing and I’m so glad they don’t have a “pay to win” option like some other apps. You have to earn the in game rewards by taking care of yourself and it’s amazing.

title: Compatible with ADHD!
body:
It is very rare that I find a self-help app that works alongside my ADHD (of course, might not the case for everyone). I have consistently opened Finch every day (with a few misses) and it wasn’t hard to get my brain into that habit; typically I would abandon (even helpful apps) an app a week in, which happened to one of the habits-as-a-game apps.

The 5 moods you can select are a great simple way to use the app, especially if you don’t have time to write. But I found that if you have the time, TAKE THE TIME to write! Finch definitely understands more detailed descriptions in my experience.

Finch, I truly cannot thank you enough for providing a service that works with my brain. I have made genuine, noticeable progress with this app and I am forever grateful.

title: FINCH FINCH FINCH
body: You will not regret this app!! I get tired of apps really quickly and I’ve been using this one everyday for nearly two months!!! The goals are flexible and you get to choose them, anything from cleaning the kitchen counters to just getting out of bed, I like the range because some days getting out of the house or out of bed is all you really can do. This tiny bird is keeping my life in check. Even if you don’t care about the goal part it has journals and reflections you can write, and it REMEMBERS people or places you wrote about on good days vs bad days!! A magic little bird, with very inclusive customization options!! I love my little finch and some days the only thing to look forward to is seeing what my finch learned that day. Thanks guys, I don’t usually write review but you two rock!!!

title: You have to pay for this app to be usable
body:
I have used this app every day for the past four months. It is very helpful and I wish I could give it a higher review because I’ve benefited greatly from it, especially with forming habits and routines, and calming down from anxiety. However, this app often causes me anxiety. I have OCD, and when I open the app on random days, all of my goals will be disorganized. I would imagine for someone without OCD, this would be annoying as well, because some goals you specifically want in the morning and some specifically later in the day, and they all get muddled. I have asked the team about this, and they “fixed” this problem by adding a feature to Finch Plus to allow you to organize goals by journeys. I don’t believe it’s fair to have that kind of organizational feature hidden behind a paywall. They have raffles that allow you to have Finch Plus for a month, but what happens when the month is up? It’s the principal of the matter. This app has actually caused me more anxiety, especially in the morning when I start my day. Its especially upsetting when I spent the previous day organizing them, and then the next day they are disorganized again. Or I’ll go a few days with all my goals in the right spot, and randomly on a day where I’m very busy, they’re all misplaced again. 

The whole point of this app is to have goals. I probably have about 30 goals meant to be completed throughout my day. Having my first goals to be halfway to the bottom is incredibly frustrating, and has often sent me into a panic attack. I know that’s a ridiculous reaction, but I have OCD. I’m debating deleting this app all together because of how frustrating this has been for me. And having the feature that would prevent this anxiety behind a paywall is unfair. This is a feature that would simply make the app usable.

title: Highly recommend
body:
The only self care app that works for me; the app is easy and quick to get the hang of, having points tied to everyday self care tasks has helped me get back into healthy habits, and I have to admit I have a paternal bond with my bird 🥰 
before downloading, I was nervous there was repercussions to not using the app or not speaking with my bird, but don’t worry if your nervous of the same thing, nothing bad can happen to your bird and you don’t lose progress or gems (the in-game currency from quests) for not keeping up with it. The only micro transactions that I’ve noticed are the subscriptions for guardians, which opens up some extra interactions but isn’t necessary and comes with multiple price options and the lowest being very affordable. If your still unable to purchase the lowest price and are unable to take advance of the free trial for whichever reason, one of the finch team gifted me a free month 💕 this was a wonderful surprise, and since then I’ve bought the subscription to continue supporting the app. Overall great app, generous and friendly team, and great vibe all around

title: I love almost all of it
body: If you’re looking for a low stress app to add to your mental health bag of wellness then this app is fantastic! The design is pleasant, the noises aren’t too loud or jarring, and there’s a good variety of journal prompts as well as different mindfulness quizzes. I also love that I don’t have to worry about checking in everyday otherwise my poor little bird dies, so that’s great! The only thing I would change is the quotes. They pop up every time you enter the app and the only way to dismiss it is to rate how you’re feeling. I’d love some more options in the settings regarding the quotes and how often you’d like to see them. Other than that, which is super inconsequential, but still a bit annoying for me personally, the app is great!

title: Finchie Falling From Grace
body:
When I started using this app (A little over 3 and a half months ago) I love love loved it! The app continued to develop in awesome ways. My quams about a daily stone cap were put to rest even, as the finch team listened to the community and fixed that issue. However, as each update went through, despite it always being for “bug fixes” broke my app more. The same issue would still occur with each update and would be worse. The app is barely usable especially if you’re not patient that day. I have to open to app, put my mood and then if I move ANYTHING on the Home Screen other than profile and neighbours it freezes until it crashes. Then I open a second time and it shows the finch loading screen longer than takes me to my home screen which is still lagging. Again, if I try to interact at all it’ll completely freeze and crash. Third times a charm I guess because at least I can get my finch on an adventure. I try to complete my goals but it will lag and freeze and crash again. Can’t spend anytime writing in the app too. 

And YES I’ve done all of the troubleshooting tips recommended already, and I’ve sent 3 bug reports as well as notified the finch team through their FB page (The finch team member commented and acknowledged it) I’m so close to uninstalling this darn thing because it causes more frustration trying to use it compared to when it worked and helped calm me down. It’s especially frustrating being told the same thing - send a bug fix, try this and that. I HAVE. My recent report has yet to even be answered and it’s been 5 days.

title: It’s ALL here: self care buffet
body: For a free app, Finch is great! It is engaging and rewarding to see my wee little bird grow. I appreciate the gender pronoun selection for my bird’s identity - but it’s a bit weird that ALL of the flags in the costume shop have to do with the rights of the 2SLGBTQI+ community. As much as I appreciate it, how about other flag ideas? I found a glitch today in the stretch activity: the images froze when I hit the “shuffle” button - a wee irritating but manageable. The soundscapes noises are also a bit irritating - lots of higher-pitched noises at a fast pace. How about a slowly-moving creek? Feels rushed. This app actually is packed with a bit too much: every self care activity most people think of is put into this app somewhere/somehow, so navigating through it all takes some time. Overall, however: 3 days after downloading Finch, I am using it at least 3 times per day. 😊 It makes me happy.

title: Cute and convenient!
body:
To start off, this app is adorable, helpful, and a great way to appreciate others in your life. 
There are many great uses that this app can supply. 

Lists!
- If you have a hobby you plan to work on, you can set daily reminders, and a personal journey along the way to help encourage and stay on track. 

Social Aspect!
- Stay in touch with your family and friends, directly, or indirectly. It’s all up to you. Invite others to join you, or have a place to simply appreciate someone not using the app.

Journeys!
- Helpful resources include: emergency help lines and calming exercises, note keeping and scheduling, personal goals and journeys towards a better self.
———————————————————————
I use the app with everyone I can convince, although I do suggest having an option along the lines of “shake for help”. Having a quick short cut to more of the emergency items. Simply a thought, but it can be very useful for people to have the option of that setting.

title: When it says to write about …
body:
If my goals are to write something I wish it would give me the chance to do so right then either before or after I check off that as a goal. So many things go together but sometimes the ‘write’ and ‘complete’ don’t seem linked.  The fewer steps involved the more likely it is to be done. Having it on my phone at my fingertips is for convenience and ease of use. The easier it is to use or link related things together, for checking off or doing, the more likely they will actually be done and I will see/feel the benefits.  Otherwise it’s a game of trying to remember to do something or check something thinking I’ll get to it and it just  ends up being something that I know I forgot or didn’t get back to. Which is a yucky feeling. 
All that being said the app is completely delightful, I love my Opal and overall worth every penny!!!  I would get it again in a heart beat and highly recommend. I hope you all keep working on growing options in all areas of the app. I’ve tried so many (and obviously didn’t work out) but this one is a gem.  Easy to use and fun.

title: I love it
body: The way i discovered this app was when my friend sent it to me and told me to get it, i had said why not and when i went to the app store i saw it was a self help kinda stuff app. I thought that it would be like every other app ive tried where it doesnt motivate me at all and that ill just give up and never use it. Usually my depression and anxiety would take over and i would never be able to take the smallest steps into a recovery. But when i got this app it was different, i knew it was different when it asked what pronouns i want my birb to be. I got excited since im very passionate about stuff like that. So moving forward ive been using this app for a while and truth be told even if i dont have plus which one day i hope to get i still am motivate everyday and ive been calmer and happier. This app has done the impossible and has led me to a healthy happy recovery. Now im still healing as my depression and anxiety wont be getting better quickly, its always gonna be a part of me but atleast i have control over it. Yes i still have hard days but my birb, who ive called lovely (they them pronouns) i still am capable of helping lovely to be energized and to go on adventures. This app is amazing for people who want to get better and i highly suggest you get this app, the fact thats its free except for the plus but you dont have to buy the plus to use the app which is amazing as other apps do make it that you only have a few days and then you have to pay. BUT with flinch im able to tall to my friends and send their birb some love and have them in my neighborhood. This app is so cute and i cant wait to keep using it🤍

body: This app sets itself far above the rest, using your bond with a cute customizable penguin to motivate you to log in frequently and play around in the app for a couple minutes or however long you want to. title: Fantastic App
body:
I love the gamification of self care. There’s a touch of nostalgia for the 90s kid in me who loved my tamagotchi like crazy. 

Also, one of the easier apps I’ve used to make goals, track them easily, and feel like I’m keeping up with them. 

So many wonderful things woven into one: coping activities for anxiety, journaling prompts that are specific or just help you let it all go, soundscapes that have honestly been a godsend with helping my newborn sleep (and now me too), celebrating achievements daily that may seem like nothing to some people but are everything to others (“step outside once”, “just survive the day”, “enjoy the warmth of a shower”). 

One of the best things I’ve found to help me keep my sanity postpartum.

title: Best addition I've ever made to my phone
body:
The new update has just about everything I was yearning for. The finch & tree town friends really make me motivated & it's the most I've stuck to a self care app. Plus it's free & the breathing features etc are fantastic. Genuinely useful. So good !!!!

I know the developers read reviews so here's some other things I wish were part of the app:

I wish you could prioritize and reorganize items in journeys/ daily lists by clicking & dragging them. 

I also wish I could add goals// to journeys etc. without adding a date or frequency. Some tasks I want to have shown from day to day without them disappearing. 
I also would like this feature for journeys so I can add a due date when It's relevant, or activate the goal so it appears on my dash. Again, I don't want to have to juggle dates and times until or unless necessary. 

 I also wish I could send friends items! 
And one day I hope there's a home/ nest option u can live in and decorate ☺️

title: 10/10 - I have the free version and I’m in love
body: I adore this app. I’ve tried so many other apps and websites for mental health and anxiety regulation but nothing has worked or helped me near as much as finch has. I think having you’re little bird friend to care of instead of yourself - as sad as that is - helps a ton (it’s like having a pet you have to feed every morning) the notifications are so cute and encouraging and have popped up at just the right time. The exercises within the app make expressing gratitude and talking about the things that bring you joy so easy especially during rough days. The breathing exercises help so much with anxiety. Having friends come and visit you just give an extra boost of motivation. Even the store and the items you can work towards are so cute and having them pop up auction style makes you excited and motivated to finish your self care activities in order to purchase the outfits you may have planned. I could honestly keep going on and on but I will cut the review here. This is just simply the BEST app - please consider checking it out I really don’t think you could ever regret it!!

title: Stop and get this!
body:
Finch is the most adorable app ever. It gives a light, cute and approachable air off to help with whatever you need to do. My friend with anxiety suggested it to me for fun, and I’m using it to boost my self confidence. Also, not to mention… your baby bird is adorable!! You get to dress them up how you want, giving total freedom of creativity. They go on the cutest adventures and come back with beautiful stories to share with you! And even if you aren’t struggling with anything, it’s a great way to check in each day or unwind to some rain or river sounds. There is a first aid tab for panic attack breathing exercises and other related things. As someone who as experienced others having panic attacks, that little tab could be so so so helpful.

Overall I think it’s a wonderful app and the intentions of the developers are beautiful 😌 thank you so much finch developers! ♥️

Ps. My birds name is kiwi 😊

title: I’m loving this app
body:
I’m very happy with this app so far; learning to easily navigate all the available features takes a bit but I wouldn’t say it’s any harder than getting a hang of most apps. 

It is a very cute, cozy app that makes self care, growth, and personal reflection feel less daunting and more like a game. 

It’s been extremely helpful for me to stay motivated, keep executive disfunction at bay, stay in a positive mindset while not making it feel like a chore (even when often it gets me doing chores) it’s helped with setting goals and getting started finding solutions and challenges that I find help with growth in the areas you choose. I know I struggle with things like feeling connected to my community or staying ontop of my self care and having suggested little steps make it much easier 

There are some features I’d love to see added, like some sort of bad habit tracker to better be able to see progress with things like lowering screen time, quitting smoking/drinking/any sort of use, self harm,  that could even be used for less problematic habits like nail chewing or just trying to cut down on things like caffeine intake, and making these features as personal input opposed to suggestions I think would keep those features from feeling suggestive.

I also would love to see an option in settings expanding on the auto tagging feature, and be able to set personal tags to auto tag for more thorough and personalized weekly data with out having to hashtag every time it’s written. 

Being able to organize and set an order to daily goals, like after making goals list being able to rearrange the order like moving tooth brushing to the top while moving sleep focus tasks to the end of the list.

And being able to set goals to repeat daily/ on certain days of the week, like being able to set drinking water and tooth brushing to every day goals or laundry to twice a week

Having a chat feature for our tree town would also be a delight 

I love this app regardless of having suggestions that I think would improve it in my mind.
 It’s helped me a lot and I have high hopes other people feel the same

title: Awesome
body:
Finch is a great app for taking care of yourself. It sends you messages throughout the day like: Lou (my finch’s name) is here for you!
It also asks how motivated you are for the day and how satisfied you were for the night. ABD it asks you why the mood change if it was an abrupt one. You can write and vent to the app In the notes and it gives you writing prompts in a way, like “what is lifting you up?”. 
There are goals and every time you complete them, you get more energy so that your finch can go on an adventure! Every time you open the app there is also a motivational quote and you can save your favourites, too. Overall, Finch is a great app and I think many people would benefit from downloading it :)

title: Amazing recovery tool
body: This is exactly what works for me. It’s so hard to find mental health apps that I connect with, but Finch is different. The journal prompts are excellent with huge variety, they’re things I never would think to ask myself. The analytic system isn’t perfect but it’s such a GENIUS feature and I can see it being so helpful as I continue to use the app over time. Tree Town is lovely, I get a message from my friend every time I open the app, and it feels like she’s cheering me on through my recovery! I grind on self improvement to get more stones for my bird’s outfit! There is such a kind tone in the entire app experience, and everyday I feel as if I’m being cheered on by the developers themselves, hehe. Love it so much. Such an incredible tool.

title: Amazing mental health and self-care app
body:
The bird is adorable, caring for the bird feels genuine but not cringe-inducing, the self-care reflective exercises are great, the guided breathing exercises are really good especially since they have an easier version, the to-do list is super motivating, and the outfits for your bird are super cute. Oh and the soundscapes! The difference to my mental health this app has made makes the paid version totally worth it, especially the cat purr soundscape, even though the free version is quite great as it is. I’ve recommended this app to many friends and talked about it positively with nearly all my healthcare workers. Thank you so much Finch team for making this great app!

The only suggestion I would have is maybe make some colours for the birds that aren’t so grey based or saturated? I would love to see pastel options for the birds.

title: the literal best
body: i was having the worst day ever today, with my mental health being so bad that i thought some really awful stuff to do for myself. but then i downloaded this app. i had quite a few friends talk about it, so i decided to see what it was all about. my pet (goofball) ‘tricks’ me into caring for them, but also myself. being scared to talk to people about my problems have led myself to be stuck with my own thoughts- but that all changed today. i now have a place to write how i feel, and how i can make myself feel better. it also helps me to complete small tasks such as showering, brushing my teeth, getting changed (etc.), and bigger things such as completing assignments and cleaning. this app helped me so much, despite me downloading it several hours ago. it’s taught me to be a better person to myself. if you’re like me, or are going through a Time, then you should absolutely download this app. if you’re reading this, then remember that i love you, and that you are cared for ❤️

title: Hands down the best self care & daily goals/habits app.
body:
I have ADHD and have tried just about every self care & habit/productivity app available but so far none had been efficient in keeping me engaged enough to comeback everyday while also not making me feel overwhelmed by reminders of things I need to do. 

The immediate mood check in when opening the app is a fantastic idea, the reminders and additional task prompts are intuitive and helpful, they offer just enough variety and options to keep me from feeling bored but also not too many that I start getting decision fatigue and bail. 

Also things are designed for you to do “right now” so you aren’t able to be like eh I’ll do it later (bc you probably won’t LOL) and I can’t recommend enough, especially if you’ve got an ADHD brain! 

Finch interactions are very chill and nurturing, and I like that nothing can be forcefully sped up, much like in RL, these things take time and are worth the wait 😊

My only issue is that I haven’t found a way to simultaneously set goals for multiple days, or copy goals from one day to paste into the next, and manually setting my goals on each individual day can be pretty tedious and time consuming.
I get that it goes with the whole “right now” vibe but if we could get a function to set up the goals for even just the week that would be a huge improvement for how I would like to be able to utilize this app more effectively. 

Other than that though it’s still 10/10 & would recommend! 😊

title: Adorable, Accessible and Effective
body:
Finch is a cutely-styled mental health app that gives you several options to lift yourself up in a given day. With options to let you feel accomplished, relaxed, excercise, and more, the app is well put together, and versatile enough to feel rewarding no matter which approach you take. 

My biggest suggestion would be to let the baby bird go on more adventures per day, since filling in tasks and quizzes and such greatly reduce the completion time, and to reduce the subscription cost per year to be more widely accessible, since the whole point is for it to be a band-aid for one’s mental health. But at the same time, the thought and effort put into this project is clear, and you deserve a bounty for such an impressive resource.

author: Nope11111

title: The best self care companion app I’ve tried so far.
body:
I don’t normally review apps much, but this one really caught my attention. As someone who struggles daily with mental health, Finch uses external motivation to get you to take care of yourself. 

Completing exercises (from breathwork to journaling to just listening to soundscapes) earns you rewards in the form of energy, cutting down on the amount of time it takes for your pet to return from their adventure.

You can earn in-app fictional currency which can be exchanged for wardrobe for your pet, and there is a daily free gift box, which is fun! You can dress up your pet however you choose.

There is also a tab where you can look at your pet’s insights! You can see how much it’s grown, what kind of personality it’s developing, and what kind of foods it likes!

Overall, this app was incredibly well thought out and designed. The plus version is a little bit on the pricier side, but it’s important to remember that there are people behind the software working to improve and maintain it. Some of you don’t value labour and it shows. Not to mention, the free version is pretty feature heavy to begin with and you can totally enjoy the app without the upgrade if it isn’t within your budget.

Thanks to the developers for making self care enjoyable. They understood the assignment: sometimes you need more than just a face mask.
